text: [clean] Cut lavender back by one-third (late August), never cutting into old, bare wood.
[clean] Pull weeds while they are still small so they never set seed across the garden.
[clean] Keep notes on which varieties thrived so next year's planting plan improves steadily.
[clean] Label each row with the variety name and sowing date in permanent ink.
[clean] Pick courgettes while they are still small and glossy, because a single forgotten marrow signals the plant to stop flowering for weeks.
[cool] Start squash seeds indoors about six weeks before the last expected frost of spring.
[cool] Sow broad beans (e.g., 'Aquadulce Claudia') in November for an early crop.
[cool] Grow tall climbing crops on the north side so that nothing ever shades the shorter rows.
[cool] Thin direct-sown beetroot to 10 cm apart.
[cool] Mulch planted rows with straw to hold moisture in the soil through dry spells.
[examine] Collect rain in large barrels during wet months so the garden has a reserve in summer.
[examine] Sharpen hoes and spades at the start of every season, because a keen edge slices through weeds with half the effort.
[examine] Never dig heavy wet clay, because treading on it ruins the soil structure for months.
[examine] Once the garlic tops fall over, lift the bulbs carefully and cure them in a dry, shaded spot for weeks.
[examine] Collect rainfall in barrels under every downpipe so the garden has a free reserve for irrigation when summer droughts arrive.

[heat] Plant onion sets firmly with the tips just showing.

[put] Keep grass paths between rows mown short so slugs have fewer spots to hide.

[put] Once the pods swell, pick peas every other day to keep the vines producing fresh pods.
[put] Save seed only from plants so the next season starts strong and true to type.
[put] Rotate crops every season so that no family grows in the same patch year after year.
[put] If seedlings stretch and topple on a bright ledge, sow the next batch more thinly and give them stronger daylight.
